description: This EPA page lists alternative air dispersion models that are not among the preferred models of the Guideline on Air Quality Models (Appendix W) but may be used in regulatory work with case-by-case justification. The models are ADAM, ADMS, AFTOX, ASPEN, BLP, CAL3QHC/CAL3QHCR, CALINE3, CALPUFF, DEGADIS, HGSYSTEM, HOTMAC/RAPTAD, HYROAD, ISC3, ISC-PRIME, OBODM, OZIPR, Panache, PLUVUEII, SCIPUFF, SDM and SLAB. Several target accidental chemical releases: DEGADIS simulates ground-level dense gas or aerosol clouds, HGSYSTEM predicts the source term and dispersion of denser-than-air releases, ADAM handles pressurised and two-phase releases, and SLAB comes with an evaluation of dense gas models; CALPUFF and SCIPUFF are puff models for tens to hundreds of kilometres. The page is maintained by EPA's Support Center for Regulatory Atmospheric Modeling and was last updated on 19 April 2026. Coverage is generic: the models apply to any site given meteorology and source data. Most code, executables, test cases and user guides are available free as zip and PDF downloads; ADMS comes from its developer and HGSYSTEM from NTIS. Caveats: many files date from the 1990s to 2012, and inclusion confers no special status. For simulation they model toxic and flammable gas releases from chemical plants, refineries and pipelines for hazard exposure and emergency response planning. It is related to the ALOHA record in this catalogue, a simpler emergency release model.
